title: Two Start-of-the-Year Questions for Educators (Teaching Simplified Series, 2022) https://davestuartjr.com/two-start-of-the-year-questions-for-educators-teaching-simplified-series-2022
author: Stuart Jr., Dave
summary: Dave uses a correspondence with a head of school, Emily Brown, as the frame for encouraging teachers to answer two start-of-year reflection questions themselves: naming a one-sentence "Everest" for what their course should produce in students, and picking one area of professional growth to focus on ("lumpy growth"). He illustrates the Everest question with real one-sentence answers from music, art, agricultural science, and Spanish teachers, and ties the growth question to the areas that most affect a teacher's Credibility with students.
points: The "Everest" exercise asks teachers to compress their course's entire purpose into a single sentence before the year starts, forcing clarity of intention.
Real teacher examples (music, art, ag science, Spanish) show the Everest sentence can be personal and discipline-specific rather than generic.
The second question — pick one area of professional growth — is framed as "lumpy growth," his term for concentrating improvement effort on a single area rather than spreading it thin.
Growth areas are explicitly tied to what most impacts teacher Credibility with students, linking self-improvement directly to the Five Key Beliefs framework.
quotes: What, in a single sentence, is your Everest this school year? If you had to boil down into a single sentence what you're hoping your class/classes/subjects produce in your students, what would that sentence be?

What one area of professional growth would you like to focus on this school year? This makes way for what I've previously called lumpy growth, and it's the most motivating method I'm aware of for growing in your expertise as a teacher.
Through teaching music and band, I can help my students become good citizens. "Good" meaning kind, responsible, problem solvers, and hard workers.

I hope that students are able to see that learning a language is a pathway to better understanding others and themselves — to learn to communicate with others who may be different from them and who may see the world through a different lens allows them to understand the world at a deeper level.
It's my contention that, while there are tons of things we can pick to improve upon as teachers, these are some of the areas that most impact our Credibility with students.
